bluf: PaperStreet is a US law firm web design and marketing agency, legal name PaperStreet Web Design, founded by a lawyer for lawyers and citing 25 years of expertise, selling attorney websites to small firms. The record knows it almost entirely from its own advertising: the site capture was unreadable and no sitemap was retrieved, so the read rests on 34 Google ads and 2 LinkedIn company ads. A rival should know that Horus puts it Exposed at -14.5 with no tailwind, and Monsoon at Landfall, 95.0, displacement 100: a web build book bought on price by small law firms, undercut line by line by an offshore rival.
doing:
PaperStreet positions, as far as its ads show, as a lawyer founded law firm web design and marketing agency pitching award winning, optimised websites that rank; the positioning line itself is marked as taken from ads because the site was unreadable. In plain words: it builds and markets websites for attorneys and leads with a free website analysis. The headline claim, again from ads, is 25 years of expertise and award winning design and marketing, founded by a lawyer for lawyers.

The sold mix is one line: web and product, scored 3, lead and core, on the legal name PaperStreet Web Design and Google and LinkedIn ads selling attorney website design and a free site analysis. SEO scores 1 with no evidence note; every other capability scores 0, breadth is 2, and the family scores put experience and build at 1.95 and search and AI visibility at 0.48 with nothing else above 0. The record holds no services list, no proprietary product, no partner badge, no CMS reading for its own site and no office.

Its AI posture is absent: the record holds no AI line, no AI search capability (P1 absent), no AI URLs and no llms.txt reading. The record lists no dated moves, no news, no case studies and no jobs. The one pricing signal is the free website analysis the Google ads offer; no price or pricing model shows. What is conspicuously absent for a legal vertical web shop of 25 years is nearly everything a record normally holds: a readable site, a sitemap, a client name, a case study, a service page, and any line beyond web design that the ads themselves do not sell. The confidence on the record is low, and the read should be treated as a read of its advertising rather than of the company.
clients:
The record reads the client type as SMB and the vertical as legal; the home market is the US, with no office listed. The needs read holds 0 clients: no case study, no logo, no press release and no slug names a law firm, and the record's evidence index is a single URL, the homepage the crawler could not read. Nothing is observed, nothing is named only and nothing is shared with another tracked agency, because there is no client to share. The only description of who it serves comes from its own ad copy: attorneys, law firms like yours, a lawyer for lawyers. For an agency citing 25 years of expertise, a public record with no named firm is the finding: the book cannot be contested by name from here, and a rival prospecting the same small law firms will not learn from this record which of them PaperStreet holds.

What the base needs next is inferred from the sold mix, since no client signal exists. Small law firms buying a website and the SEO around it sit under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), the judgment the Horus read marks PaperStreet most exposed to through its SEO line, and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), its second headwind. It is very likely, moderate confidence, that these firms will ask what an AI answer says about them and get no line from an agency with no AI capability on record, and likely, moderate confidence, that the same firms will treat a website as a priced commodity, which is what displacement 100 on the Monsoon read describes.
house: Say and do: the Radar ran no house tests on PaperStreet, so integrity is unread and no gaps were flagged; the lines it tests are not sold here beyond web design. What the record can see is its advertising, and that is steady: 34 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 21 in the last 30 days, 21 text, 8 image and 5 video, under PAPERSTREET WEB DESIGN, INC., last shown 2026-09-25, one inviting prospects to 'Contact Us for a Free Website Analysis' and another reading 'Founded by a Lawyer, for Lawyers'. LinkedIn shows 2 company page ads, one saying it helps attorneys turn their websites into optimized powerhouses and the other citing 25 years of expertise in marketing strategies for law firms. The site itself gave the record nothing: no sitemap (0 URLs, 0 updated in 90 or 365 days), no tag stack, no pixels, no test tools, no CMS reading, no llms.txt reading and no social links.
market:
Horus puts PaperStreet at tailwind index -14.5, band Exposed, percentile 5, 18:14 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum). The read lists no tailwind. It is most exposed to KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation, driven by SEO) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better, driven by SEO), both at net -0.219. Best scenario fit: The Toll Road at 62/100, with resilience 46.2. It is making none of the P moves: absent on P1, P2, P6 and P7, P5 unknown, and P3, P4 and P8 not applicable because it sells no local, paid media or paid search line.

The Monsoon read is 95.0, band Landfall, percentile 100: migration 90.0 and displacement 100.0, the ceiling. The sold mix supplies 90 of the index, Web & Product (68) and SEO (22) carrying the movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, and automation overlaps none of it. The footprint is inferred: no hub offices, no onshore claims, and the SMB client type adds 12 points.
openings:
The strongest opening is price: displacement 100.0 on the Monsoon read, with web build carrying 68 of the movable hours, says the small law firm book buys websites on price and an offshore delivered rival can very likely (high confidence) undercut the build line by line, since the record shows no onshore delivery claim, no proprietary platform and no service beyond design to defend the rate. Falsifier: a readable site or a later compile showing a productised platform, an onshore claim or a published price that an offshore delivered rival cannot beat would weaken it.

The second opening is the missing AI line: no AI search capability, no llms.txt reading and P1 absent, so a rival that sells law firm AI visibility, the thing KJ1 says replaces the click the websites are built to win, sells what PaperStreet has no ad for. No feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) leaves the machine readable layer on the sites it builds unclaimed, and no public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves an outcome priced offer unanswered. The record's silence is itself usable: a prospect asked for a PaperStreet client name, case study or result will find none in public.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and deepens the KJ1 exposure of a book built on websites that rank.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would set a public benchmark against an agency with no price on record.
The Google ads last shown 2026-09-25 with 21 of 34 in the last 30 days: whether the free website analysis campaign continues at the next compile is the only live signal the record holds.
